dense_routing.question: Does Top-1 sparse dispatch cost anything against evaluate-all-and-blend? If dense is no better, sparsity is free; if dense is much better, the canonical architecture is paying for sparsity it does not need.

primary.test: exact two-sided randomization on the difference of means
primary.verdict: SIGNIFICANT (p=0.0079, d=+1.90) -- WORSE than canonical MoRE; survives Bonferroni at 6 arms (alpha=0.0083)

fixed_depth.question: Does learned adaptive halting beat a fixed depth? T9.1 measured a depth allocation error of ~1.0 step, so the depths ACT chooses may be doing nothing that a constant could not.

primary.test: exact two-sided randomization on the difference of means
primary.verdict: SIGNIFICANT (p=0.0476, d=-1.48) -- BETTER than canonical MoRE; fails Bonferroni at 6 arms (alpha=0.0083)

routing_supervision.question: Does supervising the router with the oracle expert index improve the task metric, or only the routing metric? Canonical is 0.0 (T8.0b).

primary.test: exact two-sided randomization on the difference of means
primary.verdict: SIGNIFICANT (p=0.0079, d=+2.89) -- WORSE than canonical MoRE; survives Bonferroni at 6 arms (alpha=0.0083)

router_noise.question: Does exploration noise in the router change the partition or the loss? Canonical is none (CLAUDE.md 2). `fixed_annealed` and not `trainable`: the L2-on-trainable-noise-scale mechanism is explicitly not a proven fix, so an ablation of it would confound noise with that unproven machinery.

primary.test: exact two-sided randomization on the difference of means
primary.verdict: not significant (p=0.4107, floor 0.0179) -- supports no claim

two_blocks.question: Does a second recursive block help? Varies ONLY num_blocks -- the old 1-vs-2-block headline moved three factors at once and is uninterpretable.

primary.test: exact two-sided randomization on the difference of means
primary.verdict: not significant (p=0.7500, floor 0.0179) -- supports no claim

ponder_cost_low.question: T10.B found fixed depth BETTER than learned halting at 2.10x seed std, but [PRE-REGISTRATION -- LEFT VERBATIM. The 2.10x was a population-std artifact (T11.0a: mean_std divided by n, not n-1); corrected it is 1.88x, and under the exact randomization test that replaced the k x std rule entirely (T11.0b, code/seed_stats.py) T10.B is p = 0.125 -- NOT significant. The verdict this text rests on is withdrawn; the arm's own rationale below still holds, because 'is the coefficient mis-tuned' is worth answering whether or not fixed depth won.] that arm also raised the compute budget 2.05 -> 7.0 steps, so it cannot separate 'adaptive computation does not work' from 'our ponder cost is mis-weighted'. This arm reduces the ponder coefficient 10x (0.001 -> 0.0001) and changes NOTHING else, so halting stays adaptive and differentiable while the task term is allowed to dominate. Reading: if avg_recursion_steps rises from ~2.05 toward max_depth and val/task_loss moves to the fixed_depth number (0.062822), the ACT objective was mis-weighted and adaptive computation is viable at lower compute than fixed depth. If depth rises but loss does not follow, the halt head is not learning anything useful and Outcome C stands for the depth half of the architecture. 0.0001 and not 0.0: at zero there is no pressure to exit at all, which degenerates into T10.B and re-measures a number we already have.

primary.test: exact two-sided randomization on the difference of means
primary.verdict: not significant (p=0.1607, floor 0.0179) -- supports no claim
